checkpoints: A burst of multiple edits schedules/reset one 120 ms trailing task and writes only the latest text after 120 ms of quiet.
A later burst schedules and saves independently after the first burst has been consumed.
An empty-string edit is saved, while edit() with no current view remains a no-op.
Pending edits remain associated with the document that was current when edit() accepted them, including across open, close, dispose, and Vue unmount.
Switching or closing does not lose an accepted edit that the original immediate-write path would already have persisted.
A synchronous store listener that navigates during a save cannot let an older open operation overwrite the newer view or rendering.
Subscriptions are removed when their view retires, and status rendering remains filtered to the subscribed document ID.
createSearchPreview retains its 40 ms delay and hide cancellation behavior.

forbidden_effects: Do not continue calling env.store.write directly for every edit.
Do not cancel or discard accepted document text merely because the current view is replaced, closed, disposed, or unmounted.
Do not bind delayed text to whichever view happens to be current when the timer fires.
Do not reuse one pending trailing state across different document IDs.
Do not allow an outer open operation to install or render its destination after a synchronous save callback has initiated newer navigation.
Do not change createWorkspace/createCoordinator public operations or createSearchPreview public operations.
Do not change the search preview's 40 ms quiet interval or hide cancellation policy.
Do not change store event identity, text, revision, synchronous notification, or status-filtering semantics.
lifecycle_identity: Buffer identity is per document ID and persists independently of the current view.
The current view owns the live store subscription returned by env.store.subscribe.
Each accepted edit belongs to the buffer captured from the current view at edit() time.
Replacing or closing a view retires its subscription but must not destroy the document-owned buffer or lose accepted text.
dispose() follows close(), and Vue unmount invokes api.dispose.

obligations.text: When edit(text) has a current view, enqueue text into that view's document-specific trailing buffer instead of writing immediately to the store.
For each document, reset the trailing delay on every edit in the same burst; after 120 ms without another edit, write exactly the latest text from that burst to env.store.
After a burst is consumed, retire its pending timer/value state before invoking the synchronous store write so later or reentrant edits can form a new burst without duplicate consumption.
Keep separate reusable buffers for separate document IDs so delayed writes retain the ID of the document being edited.
Preserve accepted edits when a view is opened, replaced, closed, disposed, or unmounted; retirement must reconcile pending document work without transferring it to the successor view.
Retire the captured view's live subscription exactly once and prevent it from continuing to render status after retirement.
Because store writes and listeners are synchronous, publish retirement before a pending save can trigger navigation, and revalidate the open request before installing or rendering its destination.
Preserve document rendering from env.store.read(id), status filtering by event.id, store payload/revision behavior, and the existing public coordinator interface.
Leave createSearchPreview behavior unchanged, including its distinct 40 ms trailing task and hide cancellation.

ordering_barriers: On edit acceptance: read the current view, then push the text into that captured view's buffer; do not resolve the document ID later at timer execution.
On trailing consumption: snapshot the pending value, cancel/clear pending state, then invoke env.store.write.
On view retirement: capture the old view and revoke current ownership before callback-capable persistence or cleanup; detach the captured subscription and preserve pending document text.
On open: increment/capture the request identity, retire the previous view, recheck request authority after callback-capable retirement, then subscribe/install/render the requested document.
A synchronous navigation initiated by a store listener supersedes the older open/close operation's remaining visible effects.
preservation: createCoordinator continues to expose open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose().
Opening renders the requested document using the store's current text, subject to request authority after synchronous callbacks.
Closing clears the current view and document rendering; disposal continues to close the coordinator.
Store writes continue to update records before synchronously notifying still-subscribed listeners with {id, text, revision}.
Status events remain visible only when event.id matches the view's document ID.
The Vue component continues to expose the coordinator API and dispose it during unmount.
Search preview remains a separate transient trailing task with a 40 ms interval and cancel-on-hide behavior.
Source IDs, text values—including empty strings—and status payload semantics remain unchanged.

Vue teardown only insofar as src/Workspace.vue calls the coordinator's dispose method.
Search preview is preservation-only and receives no behavioral change.

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide().
Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.
Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription.
A store listener may call navigation synchronously.
All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

class BufferBank {constructor(){this.entries=new Map();}get(env,id){if(!this.entries.has(id))this.entries.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return this.entries.get(id);}}
edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
open(id){const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;
const buffer=bank.get(env,id),stop=env.store.subscribe(event=>{if(event.id===id)env.renderStatus(event);});setView({id,buffer,stop});env.renderDocument({id,text:env.store.read(id)});
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }

const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));
  return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};
expose(api);onBeforeUnmount(api.dispose);return{current};
